output.summary: KEP-3031 defines sigstore, with cosign as the chosen tool, as the technology the Kubernetes community uses to sign release artifacts. The KEP is implementable at stage beta.
output.rationale: The project wants a unified way to sign release artifacts that gives end users a way to verify integrity and mitigate man-in-the-middle attacks. The proposal relies on sigstore and names cosign as the tool of choice, and it is tied to the SLSA compliance effort (KEP-3027). Integration into k/release is explicitly out of scope and left to the Release Engineering subproject.

alternatives.option: Using the OCI Registry As Storage (ORAS) project
alternatives.why_not: Listed only under Alternatives in the readme; the excerpt gives no reason for not choosing it.

evidence.quote: This will be done by relying on the tools of the Linux Foundations digital signing project [sigstore]
[cosign](https://github.com/sigstore/cosign) will be the tool of our choice when speaking about the technical aspects of the solution.
How we integrate the projects into our build process in k/release is out of scope of this KEP and will be discussed in the Release Engineering subproject of SIG Release.
